name: fairy circle

attributes.attribute: left by fairy dancing on dewy grass
caused by fungus but seen as enchanted
healthy sleeper risked being carried off

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy circle is a folkloric motif. Where fairies danced, the dewy grass later showed a perfect ring. Such rings also arise from living agents, such as fungus, yet they were taken as enchanted places. Sleeping inside one was unwise, for the fairies might come back and carry off the sleeper. Cattle were steered away, since the circles were held to be poisonous for no real cause.

okr.objective: Fairy circle is a folkloric motif of enchanted and risky rings in the grass.
key_results: Fairies left a perfect circle where they danced.
Fungus caused the rings, though they seemed enchanted.
Sleeping in a circle risked being carried off.
Cattle were kept away as the rings seemed poisonous.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
